title: Uptake, translocation, and metabolism of seven frequently detected pesticides in cowpea (Vigna unguiculata L.): implications for food safety
content:
Abstract

Background

The frequent detection of multiple pesticide residues in cowpea has raised growing concerns regarding food safety and public health. This study provides the first systematic assessment of seven representative pesticides (thiamethoxam, imidacloprid, carbendazim, chlorantraniliprole, prochloraz, emamectin benzoate, pyraclostrobin) in cowpea, integrating uptake, translocation, and metabolism.

Results

All seven pesticides were rapidly taken up by roots and reached distribution equilibrium within 48–120 h. Thiamethoxam and imidacloprid preferentially accumulated in leaves with LCF > 1, whereas pyraclostrobin, prochloraz, and emamectin benzoate were predominantly retained in roots with RCF >> 1 and limited acropetal mobility. Log K ow significantly influenced pesticide accumulation in roots and leaves (R 2 = 0.8532 and 0.8734), while molecular mass mainly affected short-distance translocation within stems (R 2 = 0.7566). Pesticides with lower log K ow and smaller molecular mass were more prone to acropetal translocation. Compound-specific root uptake pathways were clarified, and 16 transformation products were tentatively identified, six of which were reported for the first time. Two prochloraz metabolites displayed markedly elevated predicted aquatic toxicity compared with the parent compound.

Conclusion

These findings deepen our understanding of the environmental behavior of multiple pesticides in cowpea, and provide a scientific basis for pesticide residue regulation, dietary risk assessment, and rational pesticide application in cowpea production. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
